doc.name: SimFuse Storefront
doc.instructions:
This server is the SimFuse eSIM storefront for AI assistants: browse
destinations and plans, price a whole trip, and open a checkout session.
No authentication is needed to read anything here.

For "which eSIM should I get for this trip?" go straight to `plan-trip`
with the stops (country code and days in each). It compares one plan
covering the whole route against one plan per country against a mix, on
live prices, and flags the cheapest complete option with a reason you can
quote verbatim. Use it whenever a trip covers two or more countries.

For a single destination: `list-destinations` to resolve the country and
its code, `get-destination-info` to describe one destination and what it
costs, `list-plans` for its plan ladder, `get-plan` for one plan's details.
For a regional or worldwide shelf: `list-regions` discovers the available
region slugs. Pass one to `list-plans` as `region`, never as `destination`.
These two filters cannot be combined. A region's members are not a promise
that every plan covers them all; check the chosen plan's actual coverage.
For "does this plan work in X?" use `check-coverage`, which answers yes or
no; `get-plan-coverage` returns the whole country list when you need it.
When the traveller says what they want rather than asking what to get
("10 GB on Docomo for two weeks, with calls"), use `build-plan`: it
returns the one real plan for that specification, snaps a shape nobody
sells to the nearest one that is, and lists every such change in
`adjustments` for you to read back. Its `plan.id` buys exactly like a
plan id from list-plans.

BUYING. Two paths, and picking the wrong one costs the sale:

- A PERSON is paying: `get-checkout-link`. It returns a page that sells
  exactly that plan with Apple Pay, Google Pay and card, takes the email at
  payment and delivers the eSIM there. No account, nothing charged by the
  call. This is the normal case.
- YOU are paying, as an agent with your own funds:
  `create-checkout-session` with the package ids plan-trip or list-plans
  returned. Nothing is charged by that call either. It returns the priced
  session with frozen totals, the payment instructions, and a bearer agent
  key; payment, completion and cancellation happen over the agentic HTTP
  API with that key, as the response's `note` describes.

AFTER THE PURCHASE. These need the order id AND the email address the order
was bought with. Both are on the buyer's confirmation email. Ask them for
both; the order id alone is refused, and a wrong pair is refused exactly as
a non-existent order is, so read nothing into which half was wrong.

- `get-order-status` - did it go through, and are the eSIMs provisioned yet.
- `get-esim-activation` - the QR code, the LPA string and the manual install
  details once they exist.
- `check-esim-usage` - how much data is used and left, per ICCID.
- `list-topup-options` - what more data would cost. READ ONLY: a top-up is
  bought in the SimFuse app, and passing those package ids to
  `create-checkout-session` would sell a second eSIM instead of filling
  this one.

Notes that will save you a wrong answer:
- Every tool returns `structuredContent` matching the `outputSchema` it
  publishes in tools/list. Read that rather than parsing the text block,
  which is the same answer serialized for clients that cannot.
- Prices are integer minor units (cents) of the currency you asked for, so
  1250 in EUR is 12.50 EUR. Pass `currency` to price in another one.
- Data allowances are megabytes; 1 GB is 1024 MB.
- A plan id comes from a tool response or the product feed. Never invent
  one, and never guess a destination code, look it up.
- Quotes and sessions are offers, not reservations: the charged total is
  always computed at checkout, and a session's prices are only frozen
  until its `price_locked_until`.
- Provisioning is dispatched, not awaited, so an order can be paid for
  before its eSIM exists. An empty `esims` list moments after payment means
  wait and ask again, never that something failed.
- Usage readings come from a cache refreshed every couple of minutes.
  `checked_at` says how old the number is; do not present it as live.
- We do not publish which network operator or upstream supplier a plan
  runs on beyond the carrier and network type already in the response. If
  asked, say that rather than inferring it.

tools.name: plan-trip
tools.title: Plan eSIMs for a trip
tools.description: Answer "which eSIM should I buy for this trip?". Give it the stops, a country code and the days spent in each, and it compares one plan covering the whole route against one plan per country against a mix of the two, on live prices, then flags the cheapest option that covers everything and explains the choice in a sentence you can quote. It also estimates the data each stop needs, names any country SimFuse cannot cover, and returns package ids that go straight into create-checkout-session. Use it whenever a trip has two or more countries, and for a single country when the traveller wants a recommendation rather than a list. Read-only: nothing is reserved and nothing is charged, and the totals are today's catalog prices, not a quote held for later.

stops.description: The trip, one entry per country, in travel order. 1 to 12 stops, e.g. [{"country":"JP","days":7},{"country":"KR","days":5}].

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. "JP" for Japan. Look one up with list-destinations rather than guessing. Each country may appear once: give one stop with the total days rather than two visits.

days.description: Days spent in that country, 1 to 365. Count the nights of the stay.

usage.description: Optional. How heavily data is used during this stop: "light" (about 300 MB a day, maps and messaging), "regular" (about 800 MB a day) or "heavy" (about 2 GB a day, video and hotspot). Overrides the trip-wide `usage` for this stop only.
Optional. Trip-wide data usage for stops that do not set their own: "light" (about 300 MB a day), "regular" (about 800 MB a day) or "heavy" (about 2 GB a day). Defaults to "regular".

start.description: Optional. Departure date as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-04-18". Only used to date the stops in the answer; it does not change prices. Defaults to today.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code every price is quoted in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

contract.description: Version of this answer's shape. "1" today; it only changes when an existing field changes meaning.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code every amount below is quoted in, e.g. "EUR".

trip.description: The trip as it was understood, which is worth reading back to the traveller.

token.description: Compact encoding of the trip, for the planner_url link.

start.description: First day of the trip, YYYY-MM-DD.

end.description: Last day of the trip, YYYY-MM-DD.

span_days.description: Total days from arrival at the first stop to departure from the last.

stops.description: The stops, in travel order, with their dates and data estimates.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the stop.

usage.description: The data appetite used for this stop.

estimated_mb.description: Data this stop is estimated to need, in megabytes (1 GB is 1024 MB).

estimated_data.description: The same estimate written for a person, e.g. "3.9 GB".

recommendation.description: Which strategy won: one plan for the whole route, one plan per country, or a mix. Null when nothing we sell covers the trip.

reason.description: One sentence explaining the recommendation, written to be quoted to the traveller verbatim.

options.description: Every way of buying the trip that we could price, cheapest-first within each strategy. Empty when nothing we sell covers it.

strategy.description: How this option buys the trip.

recommended.description: True on the one option this answer recommends.

esims.description: How many eSIMs the traveller installs under this option.

total_cents.description: Total price in minor units (cents) of the response currency, so 2450 is 24.50.

total.description: The same total formatted for a person, e.g. "24.50 EUR".

complete.description: True when this option covers every stop. False means at least one stop is left without data.

purchasable.description: False when the option needs more eSIMs than one order can carry.

saves_cents.description: What this option saves against the next cheapest complete alternative, in minor units. 0 when there is none or when it is dearer.

package_id.description: The plan id to buy. Pass it to create-checkout-session or get-plan.

name.description: Plan name as a traveller sees it.

covers.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of the stops this line covers.

quantity.description: How many of this plan to buy.

data.description: Allowance written for a person, e.g. "5 GB" or "Unlimited".

data_mb.description: Allowance in megabytes. 0 on an unlimited plan, where `policy` carries the real terms.

unlimited.description: True when the plan is sold as unlimited, which almost always means unlimited up to a fair-use cap.

validity_days.description: How many days the plan stays valid once it activates.

policy.description: What the plan really gives you. Null when the supplier has never published its terms, which is different from having no limits.

high_speed_data_mb.description: Full-speed allowance in megabytes PER RESET PERIOD, so 1 GB a day for 30 days is 1024, not 30720. 0 means genuinely uncapped.

reset_period.description: How often the full-speed allowance resets. Null means it covers the whole plan.

max_speed_kbps.description: Speed ceiling in kbit/s from the first megabyte. Null means no ceiling.

reduced_speed_kbps.description: Speed in kbit/s after the full-speed allowance is used. Null means the data STOPS rather than slowing down.

price_cents.description: Price for one of this plan, in minor units (cents) of the response currency.

price.description: The same price formatted for a person.

warnings.description: What this option does not do: a stop it leaves uncovered, a plan that runs out or expires early. Empty when there is nothing to say.
Trip-level caveats: a country SimFuse does not sell, or a gap the recommended option leaves. Say these out loud rather than dropping them.

planner_url.description: The same trip on the SimFuse website, for a person who wants to finish it themselves.

checkout.description: How to act on the recommendation.

items.description: The recommended option as checkout line items, ready to pass to create-checkout-session. Null when nothing covers the trip.

checkout_sessions.description: HTTP endpoint that opens a checkout session, if you would rather not use the create-checkout-session tool.

register.description: HTTP endpoint that mints an agent key for that API.

human_url.description: Where to send a person to buy this themselves.

note.description: What the totals are and are not: catalog prices today, never a reservation.

tools.name: list-destinations
tools.title: List eSIM destinations
tools.description: Find the countries SimFuse sells eSIMs for, with the cheapest plan price ("from" price) for each in the currency you ask for. Start here when someone names a place: it turns "Portugal" into the two-letter country code the other tools take, and shows what that destination starts at. For one destination, follow it with list-plans; for a trip covering two or more countries, use plan-trip instead. Read-only, and it answers from the SimFuse catalog alone.

search.description: Optional. Match destinations by name, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 code, case-insensitively. A partial name works: "port" matches Portugal. Omit to list every destination.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code the "from" prices are quoted in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum destinations to return, 1 to 300. Defaults to 300, which is the whole list.

total.description: How many destinations matched, before `limit` was applied.

returned.description: How many destinations are in this response.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code every from_price_cents below is quoted in, e.g. "EUR".

destinations.description: The matching destinations. Empty when nothing matched.

iso2.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. "ES". This is the code list-plans and plan-trip take.

region.description: The region this country is filed under, e.g. "Europe". Null when it is filed under none.

from_price_cents.description: Cheapest plan for this destination, in minor units (cents) of the response currency, so 1250 is 12.50. Null when this response did not price the destination.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code the from_price_cents beside it is expressed in, which is the currency you asked for, e.g. "EUR". Null exactly when from_price_cents is null, which is what a country nested on a plan answers: nothing priced it there.

path.description: Path on the storefront, e.g. "/esim/spain/". Always the canonical page, never a redirect.

query.description: Query parameters that belong on the path, as an object. Empty when there are none.

url.description: The full storefront URL for this country's storefront page. Safe to show to a person.

tools.name: list-regions
tools.title: List eSIM regions
tools.description: Discover available eSIM regions, including worldwide scopes, with their canonical slugs, display names, member countries and starting prices. Only published regions with active displayed regional plans are listed. Pass a returned region slug to list-plans as region, not destination. Country membership describes the region, not a promise that every plan covers every member: check get-plan-coverage for a specific plan. Read-only; no account or key is needed.

search.description: Optional. Case-insensitive partial match on the canonical region slug or display name, e.g. "asia". Omit to list all available regions.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 code for starting prices, e.g. "EUR" or "USD". Defaults to EUR; unknown codes fall back to the base currency.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum regions to return, 1 to 300. Defaults to 300. total reports the match count before this limit.

returned.description: Number of regions in this response.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for all starting prices.

regions.description: Available regions in storefront order. Empty when nothing matches.

region.description: Canonical slug to pass to list-plans.region.

countries.description: Region membership as ISO2 codes, not the coverage of any one plan. Empty for worldwide scopes.

countries_count.description: Region size by catalog taxonomy. Do not use this as an individual plan coverage count.

plan_countries_count.description: Widest single plan coverage. Say "up to" this many countries; the cheapest plan may cover fewer.

from_price_cents.description: Cheapest displayed regional plan price in minor units of currency, e.g. 1250 means EUR 12.50 when currency is EUR.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for from_price_cents.

tools.name: get-destination-info
tools.title: Get destination info
tools.description: Details for one destination: its name and codes, region, how many eSIM plans are sold there, the cheapest and most expensive, the smallest and largest data bundles, and its storefront page. Takes a country name ("Japan") or two-letter code ("JP"). Use this to describe a destination before pulling its full plan ladder with list-plans. Whether a plan can be topped up varies by plan and is reported by list-plans, not here.

destination.description: The destination: a country name ("Japan") or a two-letter code ("JP").

currency.description: Three-letter currency code for the prices (e.g. "USD", "EUR"). Defaults to EUR.

iso2.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. "JP". This is the code list-plans and plan-trip take.

region.description: The region this country is filed under, e.g. "Asia". Null when it is filed under none.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code every amount below is quoted in, e.g. "EUR".

count.description: How many plans are sold for this destination.

lowest_price_cents.description: Cheapest plan, in minor units (cents), so 1250 is 12.50.

smallest_bundle_mb.description: Smallest metered allowance in megabytes. Unlimited plans store 0 MB and are counted in the price range and the plan count but not here, so this is 0 when every plan is unlimited.

largest_bundle_mb.description: Largest metered allowance in megabytes, on the same terms.

path.description: Path on the storefront, e.g. "/esim/spain/". Always the canonical page, never a redirect.

query.description: Query parameters that belong on the path, as an object. Empty when there are none.

url.description: The full storefront URL for this country's storefront page. Safe to show to a person.

note.description: How to read the numbers above, and what to call next.

tools.name: list-plans
tools.title: List eSIM plans
tools.description: Show the eSIM plans on sale for one country or region, or search the whole catalog, narrowing by data allowance, validity and price. Use destination with a country code from list-destinations, or region with a slug from list-regions; never both. Use it when the traveller wants to compare what is available or find a plan inside a budget. Prices are live retail prices in the currency you ask for. For a trip covering two or more countries, use plan-trip first: it compares one plan for the whole route against one plan per country and picks the cheapest complete answer. Pass a plan id from here to get-plan, get-plan-coverage or create-checkout-session. Read-only, and it answers from the SimFuse catalog alone.

destination.description: Optional. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 destination country code, e.g. "US", "GB", "DE". Look it up with list-destinations rather than guessing. Cannot be combined with region. Omit both destination and region to search the whole catalog.

region.description: Optional. Canonical region slug, e.g. "europe", "southeast-asia" or "global", to search that regional shelf. Cannot be combined with destination. Unknown regions return no plans.

min_data_amount_mb.description: Optional. Only plans with at least this much data, in MEGABYTES: 1 GB is 1024, 10 GB is 10240.

max_data_amount_mb.description: Optional. Only plans with at most this much data, in megabytes.

min_validity_days.description: Optional. Only plans valid for at least this many days, e.g. 14 for a two-week trip.

max_validity_days.description: Optional. Only plans valid for at most this many days.

min_price_cents.description: Optional. Only plans at or above this retail price, in minor units (cents) of `currency`: 500 is 5.00.

max_price_cents.description: Optional. Only plans at or below this retail price, in minor units (cents) of `currency`: 2500 is 25.00.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code prices are quoted and filtered in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum plans to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

matched.description: How many plans matched the filters, before `limit` was applied.

returned.description: How many plans are in this response.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code every price below is quoted in, e.g. "EUR".

truncated_by_candidate_cap.description: True when a catalog-wide search hit its internal candidate cap, so there are further matches this call could not see. Narrow it with a destination or a tighter data or validity filter rather than assuming you have seen everything.

plans.description: The matching plans. Empty when nothing matched.

id.description: The plan id (a 26-character ULID). Pass it to get-plan, get-plan-coverage or create-checkout-session. Never invent one.

name.description: Plan name as a traveller sees it, e.g. "Spain 5GB".

carrier.description: The mobile network this plan runs on, when we can name it. Null when we cannot.

network.description: The network name as plain text, or null when unknown.

operators.description: Network operators the plan roams on, as a list. Empty when none are published.

data_amount_mb.description: Data allowance in megabytes (1 GB is 1024 MB). 0 on an unlimited plan, where data_usage_policy carries the real terms.

data_usage_policy.description: What the plan really gives you. Null when the supplier has never published its terms, which is different from having no limits.

high_speed_data_mb.description: Full-speed allowance in megabytes PER RESET PERIOD, so 1 GB a day for 30 days is 1024, not 30720. 0 means genuinely uncapped.

reset_period.description: How often the full-speed allowance resets. Null means it covers the whole plan.

max_speed_kbps.description: Speed ceiling in kbit/s from the first megabyte. Null means no ceiling.

reduced_speed_kbps.description: Speed in kbit/s after the full-speed allowance is used. Null means the data STOPS rather than slowing down.

hotspot_usage_policy.description: What the plan lets you do with a hotspot. Null when the terms were never established, which is different from being allowed.

allowed.description: Whether the plan may be shared as a hotspot at all.

high_speed_data_mb.description: A separate tethering allowance in megabytes per reset period. Null means tethering draws on the plan data with no allowance of its own.

reset_period.description: How often the tethering allowance resets. Null when it covers the whole plan.

max_speed_kbps.description: Speed ceiling in kbit/s while tethering. Null means no ceiling.

reduced_speed_kbps.description: Speed in kbit/s once the tethering allowance is used. Null means tethering stops.

max_total_mb.description: A hard cap on tethered data across the whole plan, in megabytes. Null means no such cap.

validity_days.description: How many days the plan stays valid once it activates.

type.description: What the plan sells: data only, or data plus a bundled voice and SMS allowance.

data_restriction_type.description: Whether the allowance is capped ("limited") or unmetered ("unlimited").

coverage_type.description: Scope of the plan: one country, a region, or worldwide.

region.description: Raw region value for a regional plan, e.g. "Europe". Null for a country plan.

region_label.description: The region formatted for a person to read. Null for a country plan.

is_worldwide.description: True when the plan is sold as a worldwide bundle.

coverage_countries.description: Every country the plan works in.

iso2.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, or null for a country we could not match to a code.

operators.description: Networks in that country, when the country could be attributed. Empty means not attributed, never "no coverage".

excluded_countries.description: Countries in this plan's own region that it does NOT cover. Always empty for a country plan and for a worldwide one.

retail_price_cents.description: Retail price in minor units (cents) of `currency`, so 1250 in EUR is 12.50 EUR. This is what a buyer pays for one eSIM.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code retail_price_cents is quoted in, e.g. "EUR".

retail_prices_cents.description: Prices in other currencies, keyed by ISO 4217 code, in minor units. Only the multi-currency surfaces (the catalog export) carry one, so it is absent here: read retail_price_cents and currency instead.

supports_topup.description: Whether more data can be bought for the same eSIM once it runs low.

supports_tethering.description: Whether hotspot or tethering is allowed. Null means no supplier has declared it, which is not the same as "no".

network_type.description: Deprecated two-valued form: "5G" for a 5G plan, "LTE" for everything else including plans whose generation was never stated. Read network_generation.

network_generation.description: The network generation the plan is sold as, exactly as stated for it. Null means not stated, which is not the same as any generation; say "not stated" rather than assuming.

country.description: The one country this plan is filed under. Null for a regional or worldwide plan.

iso2.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. "ES". This is the code list-plans and plan-trip take.

region.description: The region this country is filed under, e.g. "Europe". Null when it is filed under none.

from_price_cents.description: Cheapest plan for this destination, in minor units (cents) of the response currency, so 1250 is 12.50. Null when this response did not price the destination.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code the from_price_cents beside it is expressed in, which is the currency you asked for, e.g. "EUR". Null exactly when from_price_cents is null, which is what a country nested on a plan answers: nothing priced it there.

path.description: Path on the storefront, e.g. "/esim/spain/". Always the canonical page, never a redirect.

query.description: Query parameters that belong on the path, as an object. Empty when there are none.

url.description: The full storefront URL for this country's storefront page. Safe to show to a person.

links.description: Where a person buys this plan on simfuse.app.

path.description: Path on the storefront, e.g. "/esim/spain/". Always the canonical page, never a redirect.

query.description: Query parameters that belong on the path, as an object. Empty when there are none.

url.description: The full storefront URL for the page this plan is bought on, with the plan preselected. Safe to show to a person.

country.description: The country page on its own, or null when the plan has no single country.

path.description: Path on the storefront, e.g. "/esim/spain/". Always the canonical page, never a redirect.

query.description: Query parameters that belong on the path, as an object. Empty when there are none.

url.description: The full storefront URL for the plan's country page. Safe to show to a person.

tools.name: get-plan
tools.title: Get eSIM plan details
tools.description: Read everything about one eSIM plan by its id: data allowance, how long it stays valid, what happens after a fair-use cap, whether hotspot and top-ups are supported, the network it runs on, and the retail price in the currency you ask for. Use it to answer a specific question about a plan already found with list-plans or plan-trip, and before buying, to confirm the plan really matches what the traveller asked for. Ask get-plan-coverage instead when the question is which countries it works in. Read-only: it reserves nothing and charges nothing.

tools.name: build-plan
tools.title: Build an eSIM plan
tools.description: Build an eSIM plan to the traveller's liking for one destination: how much data, for how many days, optionally which network it runs on and whether calls and texts are bundled. Returns the one real plan that matches, with its id and live price, never a made-up combination: a shape nobody sells is snapped to the nearest one that is, one axis at a time, and every change is spelled out in `adjustments` so you can read it back. Use it when the traveller knows what they want ("10 GB on Docomo for two weeks"); use plan-trip when they want a recommendation or the trip has several countries. To buy, pass `plan.id` to get-checkout-link when a person is paying, or to create-checkout-session when you are. Read-only: it reserves nothing and charges nothing.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the destination, e.g. "JP". Look it up with list-destinations rather than guessing.

data_mb.description: Data allowance wanted, in megabytes: 1 GB is 1024 MB, so 5 GB is 5120. Pass 0 for an unlimited plan. Snapped to the nearest size sold when no plan has exactly this size.

validity_days.description: How many days the plan should stay valid, 1 to 365. Snapped to the nearest length sold for the chosen size.

network.description: Optional. The mobile network the plan should run on, by carrier name as `options.networks` lists them, e.g. "NTT Docomo" or "au". Matching is case-insensitive and a single carrier of a multi-network plan is enough. Omit for the cheapest network.

voice.description: Optional. True to require a plan that bundles calls and texts. Defaults to false, data only. If no such plan exists the answer is data only and says so.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code the price is quoted in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

tools.name: get-checkout-link
tools.title: Get checkout link
tools.description: Get the page where a person buys one specific eSIM plan, for an assistant to hand them a link. The page sells exactly this plan with Apple Pay, Google Pay and card, takes the email at payment, and sends the eSIM there. Nothing is charged or reserved by this call and the buyer needs no account. Use this whenever a PERSON is going to pay. Use create-checkout-session instead when the agent is settling the purchase itself, or for more than one plan or unit.

plan_id.description: The plan id (a ULID) as returned by list-plans, get-plan or plan-trip.

currency.description: Three-letter currency code for the price quoted back to you (e.g. "USD", "EUR"). Defaults to EUR. The page itself prices in the buyer's own currency.

source.description: The name of the assistant or app sending the buyer, recorded as the campaign source on the link (e.g. "claude"). Optional.

url.description: The page to give the buyer. Opens the plan with Apple Pay, Google Pay and card on it. Safe to show to a person.

id.description: The plan id (a 26-character ULID) this link buys.

name.description: Plan name as a traveller sees it, e.g. "Spain 5GB".

data_amount_mb.description: Full-speed allowance in megabytes; 1 GB is 1024 MB. 0 on an unlimited plan.

data_restriction_type.description: "limited" for a metered allowance, "unlimited" for one sold as uncapped.

validity_days.description: Days the plan stays valid once activated.

coverage_count.description: How many countries the plan works in.

price_cents.description: Indicative price in minor units (cents) of the currency below, so 1250 is 12.50. The page prices live in the buyer's own currency and that is what is charged.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code price_cents is quoted in, e.g. "EUR".

note.description: What the buyer will see on that page, in words you can repeat to them.

tools.name: create-checkout-session
tools.title: Create checkout session
tools.description: Open a checkout session for one or more eSIM plans at frozen prices, using the plan ids that plan-trip, list-plans or get-plan returned. Use it once the traveller has chosen what to buy. It CHARGES NOTHING and reserves no stock: it prices the basket, freezes those prices until the session's price_locked_until, and hands back the session plus a bearer agent key. Payment, completion and cancellation happen afterwards over the SimFuse agentic HTTP API with that key, as the session's `note` explains, and the eSIM is delivered by email once payment settles. Each call opens a NEW session and mints a NEW key, so call it once per basket rather than retrying it to re-read one.

items.description: What to buy: one entry per plan, 1 to 50 entries. Pass the whole basket in one call, e.g. [{"id":"01JVQ...","quantity":1}].

id.description: A plan id (26-character ULID) from plan-trip, list-plans, get-plan or the product feed, e.g. "01JVQ2S6D4X8N0RMB7YQZ5K3TA". Never invent one.

quantity.description: How many of this plan to buy, 1 to 20. One eSIM per unit, so 2 means two separate eSIMs of the same plan (one traveller normally needs 1).

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code to price the session in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. Every amount in the answer is minor units (cents) of this currency.

buyer_email.description: Optional but strongly recommended. The traveller's email address, where the eSIM and its installation details are sent once payment settles. Ask for it rather than inventing one.

agent_name.description: Optional. Name of the assistant or app opening the session, e.g. "Claude". Recorded on the agent key so we can tell integrations apart. Defaults to "mcp-client".

session.description: The priced checkout session, in the same shape the agentic HTTP API returns it.

id.description: Session id, used in every follow-up call.

protocol.description: Agentic Commerce Protocol version this session speaks.

status.description: Where the session is: "ready_for_payment" means it can be completed; "complete_in_progress" means payment has not settled yet and the purchase is NOT done; "completed" means the eSIM is on its way. Also "incomplete", "not_ready_for_payment", "canceled" and "expired".

currency.description: Lower-case ISO 4217 code every amount is in, e.g. "eur".

line_items.description: One entry per plan in the basket.

id.description: The plan id bought on this line.

base_amount.description: Price of one unit, in minor units.

totals.description: The money, ordered so the lines read down to the total.

display_text.description: The line written for a person.

amount.description: Amount in minor units (cents) of the session currency. A discount is NEGATIVE, so the lines sum to the total.

fulfillment_options.description: How the eSIM is delivered. Instant and free, stated explicitly so nobody has to guess whether shipping is coming.

type.description: Always "digital" here: an eSIM has nothing to ship.

description.description: What the traveller receives, and when.

display_text.description: The line written for a person.

amount.description: Amount in minor units (cents) of the session currency. A discount is NEGATIVE, so the lines sum to the total.

handlers.description: The ways this session can be paid.

id.description: Handler id to name when completing the session.

requires_delegate_payment.description: Whether the agent must mint a delegated payment token first.

requires_pci_compliance.description: Whether card data passes through the agent.

settlement.description: "synchronous" settles during completion; "asynchronous" settles later, so a 200 is not yet a purchase.

default_asset.description: Default asset for a crypto handler.

buyer.description: The buyer, when one was given. Null when no email was supplied, in which case ask for one before completing.

payment_handler_id.description: The handler this session will settle through.

messages.description: Anything the agent must read before completing: payment instructions, a gateway minimum this basket does not clear, or a warning that settlement is still pending.

type.description: Whether this is information or a caution.

content_type.description: "application/json" when `content` is an object, "text/plain" when it is a sentence.

content.description: The message itself. Payment instructions arrive here as fields (address, exact amount, memo): pass them through EXACTLY, never reformatted or rounded.

links.description: Seller policies, for a buyer who asks.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp after which this session can no longer be completed.

price_locked_until.description: ISO 8601 timestamp until which these totals hold. After it, re-read the session for fresh totals rather than quoting these.

order.description: The order this session produced, once it has one. Null until then.

agent_key.description: The bearer key for every follow-up call on this session, shown ONCE and never again. Send it as "Authorization: Bearer <key>". It is a credential: use it, do not read it out to the traveller.

api.description: The HTTP endpoints for this session, all taking the agent_key as a bearer token.

session.description: GET this to re-read the session and its current totals.

complete.description: POST here to complete the purchase, which is where payment happens.

cancel.description: POST here to cancel the session.

note.description: How to use the key and how long the prices hold. Worth following literally.

tools.name: get-order-status
tools.title: Get order status
tools.description: Check an eSIM order after payment: whether it completed and whether its eSIMs have been provisioned yet. Identified by the order id together with the email that bought it, both of which are on the buyer's confirmation email. Provisioning usually finishes within a minute of payment, so an order that is paid but lists no eSIMs yet is normal: check again shortly. Once an eSIM is listed, use get-esim-activation to fetch its QR code and install details.

order_id.description: The order id from the buyer's confirmation email or order page.

email.description: The email address the order was bought with. Required: the order id alone does not identify a buyer.

status.description: Order state, e.g. "completed" or "pending". "completed" is about the eSIM having provisioned, not about the money.

placed_at.description: When the order was created, ISO 8601. Null on the rare row that has no timestamp.

esims.description: Every eSIM provisioned on this order. EMPTY while provisioning is still in flight, which is normal for the first minute after payment and never means the order failed.

iccid.description: The eSIM's ICCID. Pass it to check-esim-usage or list-topup-options.

status.description: eSIM state, e.g. "active", "pending", "expired". Null before the supplier has reported one.

note.description: What to do next, given the list above.

tools.name: get-esim-activation
tools.title: Get eSIM activation details
tools.description: Fetch the installable eSIM(s) for a paid order: the QR code image, the LPA activation string, the SM-DP+ address and activation code for manual entry, one-tap install links for iPhone and Android, and a hosted install page to send the buyer. Identified by the order id together with the email that bought it. Returns an empty esims list while provisioning is still in flight, which normally clears within a minute of payment.

order_id.description: The order id from the buyer's confirmation email or order page.

email.description: The email address the order was bought with. Required: the order id alone does not identify a buyer.

esims.description: Every eSIM on this order. EMPTY while provisioning is still in flight.

status.description: eSIM state, e.g. "active". Null before the supplier has reported one.

activation_code.description: The activation code, for entering the profile by hand. Null before provisioning finishes.

smdp_address.description: The SM-DP+ server address, the other half of a manual install. Null before provisioning finishes.

lpa.description: The GSMA activation string, "LPA:1$smdp$code". Null when the details cannot form a valid payload, which is the case you handle by falling back to the two fields above.

apple_link.description: One-tap install on iOS. Open it ON the device that will use the eSIM. Null whenever lpa is.

android_link.description: One-tap install on Android, on the same terms.

qr_code_url.description: The install QR as a self-contained data: URI, so it can be rendered without a second fetch. Null whenever lpa is.

install_url.description: A hosted install page, signed and safe to send a person. The same page the app and the activation email link to.

note.description: How to get the profile onto the traveller's phone.

tools.name: check-esim-usage
tools.title: Check eSIM data usage
tools.description: How much data an eSIM has used and how much is left, for one eSIM on a paid order. Identified by the order id and the email that bought it, plus the ICCID from get-order-status or get-esim-activation. Allowances are in megabytes. Readings are served from a cache refreshed every couple of minutes: checked_at says when the reading was taken. An unlimited plan reports its full-speed allowance for the current period rather than a total.

order_id.description: The order id from the buyer's confirmation email or order page.

email.description: The email address the order was bought with.

iccid.description: The ICCID of the eSIM to read, as returned by get-order-status.
The eSIM this reading belongs to.

status.description: eSIM state at the time of the reading, e.g. "active".

is_unlimited.description: Whether the plan is sold as unlimited. Almost none are uncapped: see the period fields for what that actually means here.

data_used_mb.description: Megabytes used on the current bundle; 1 GB is 1024 MB.

data_remaining_mb.description: Megabytes left. NULL on an unmetered plan, which does not mean zero: it means the supplier reports no allowance to count down.

data_total_mb.description: Size of the current bundle in megabytes, reflecting any top-ups. Null on an unmetered plan.

percentage_used.description: Share of the bundle spent, 0-100. Null on an unmetered plan, where there is no total to be a share of.

percentage_remaining.description: Share of the bundle left, 0-100. Null on the same terms.

period_remaining_mb.description: Full-speed data left in the CURRENT reset period, for a plan whose allowance refills (say 3 GB a day). Null when the plan has no reset period. Deliberately separate from data_remaining_mb, which describes the whole plan.

period_high_speed_mb.description: Size of that period allowance, so the figure above can be read as "945 MB of 3 GB left today".

period_reset.description: How often it refills: "daily", "weekly" or "monthly". Null when it does not.

period_reduced_speed_kbps.description: Speed the plan throttles to once the period allowance is spent. NULL means the data STOPS instead, which is a different thing to tell a traveller.

checked_at.description: When this reading was TAKEN, ISO 8601. Readings come from a cache refreshed every couple of minutes, so do not present the number as live.

activated_at.description: When the eSIM first connected, ISO 8601. Null before activation.

expires_at.description: When the plan lapses, ISO 8601. Null when the supplier reports none.

tools.name: list-topup-options
tools.title: List top-up options
tools.description: Data top-ups that can be added to an eSIM the buyer already has, narrowed to what its network will actually accept. Identified by the order id and the email that bought it, plus the ICCID. Read-only: a top-up is bought in the SimFuse app, not through this server, and the response carries the link that opens this eSIM there. Do not pass these package ids to create-checkout-session, which would buy a separate new eSIM rather than add data to this one.

email.description: The email address the order was bought with.

iccid.description: The ICCID of the eSIM to top up, as returned by get-order-status.

iccid.description: The eSIM these options apply to.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code every price below is quoted in, e.g. "EUR".

data_amount_mb.description: Allowance this top-up adds, in megabytes.

high_speed_data_mb.description: Full-speed allowance in megabytes PER RESET PERIOD, so 1 GB a day for 30 days is 1024, not 30720. 0 means genuinely uncapped.

reset_period.description: How often the full-speed allowance resets. Null means it covers the whole plan.

max_speed_kbps.description: Speed ceiling in kbit/s from the first megabyte. Null means no ceiling.

reduced_speed_kbps.description: Speed in kbit/s after the full-speed allowance is used. Null means the data STOPS rather than slowing down.

retail_price_cents.description: Price in minor units (cents), so 1250 is 12.50.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the price beside it.

is_same_package.description: Whether this is the plan the eSIM is running now (its latest top-up, or the plan it was bought on if never topped up). Topping up this plan adds to the data the eSIM has left, which is the usual "more of the same" choice.

replaces_current_plan.description: Whether buying this option REPLACES the plan the eSIM is running now, so any data left on it is lost for good instead of being added to. When true, warn the customer before they buy, and suggest the option with is_same_package true if they want to keep their remaining data.

available_over_mcp.description: Always false. A top-up charge is protected by device checks this connection cannot produce.

open_in_app.description: A link that opens this eSIM in the SimFuse app, where the top-up is actually bought. Safe to send a person.

note.description: What to tell the buyer, and what not to do with the ids above.
